place.source_title: Nicholas Dowling Building, Diagonal & Main Streets

brief: Four-storey brick commercial building of about 1840 on a steep corner, plain Federal walls with stone lintels, an ornate cast-iron balcony across the second floor, and a 1931 storefront at street level; the uphill side shows its full height.

facade.notes: the Nicholas Dowling Building (Galena, c.1840): a narrow four-storey brick building at a corner on a steep street, a wooden balcony over the shop sign 'FRED ORTSGHEID & SON', a stone retaining wall climbing beside it; feed sacks on the sidewalk

why.note: the two-part block: business below, offices or rooms above
Galena's bluff: the side street climbs on a stone wall
